V04 shelf-gap events → targeted re-scans
order picks → delivery tasks
C03 instant-retail orders → picking + handoff" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="106" width="440" x="20" y="44" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="k2" parent="work" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=8;fontStyle=1" value="driven by dim_calendar, so 双11 / 春节 peaks are
SIMULATED, not averaged away" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="48" width="440" x="20" y="160" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="k3" parent="work" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f3faf1;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=8;fontStyle=1" value="Anyone can simulate robots driving around.
Feeding it our ACTUAL event history is what makes
the answer credible:

"three robots, to keep 95th-percentile task latency
under 20 minutes on the week of 双11"

— a sentence a CFO can act on." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="98" width="440" x="20" y="218" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ans" parent="1" style="swimlane;startSize=34;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;fillColor=#faf7fc;strokeColor=#9673a6;fontStyle=1;fontSize=12;fontColor=#6b4c85;" value="ANSWERS the twin produces" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="280" width="480" x="520" y="470" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n1" parent="ans" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#e1d5e7;strokeColor=#9673a6;fontSize=11;fontStyle=1" value="robots needed for a given SLA → the curve" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="34" width="440" x="20" y="44" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n2" parent="ans" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#e1d5e7;strokeColor=#9673a6;fontSize=11;" value="route feasibility · scan time per store" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="34" width="440" x="20" y="86" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n3" parent="ans" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#e1d5e7;strokeColor=#9673a6;fontSize=11;" value="deadlock hotspots → where to put mutex groups" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="34" width="440" x="20" y="128" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n4" parent="ans" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#e1d5e7;strokeColor=#9673a6;fontSize=11;" value="charge-window planning · task latency distribution" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="34" width="440" x="20" y="170" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="n5" parent="ans" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#ffe6cc;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=11;fontStyle=1" value="COST PER TASK at vendor price points
goods-to-person carriers $25k–50k/unit,
transport AMRs $25k–80k → the capital business case" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="56" width="440" x="20" y="212" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="pick" parent="1" style="swimlane;startSize=34;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;fillColor=#f9f9f9;strokeColor=#999999;fontStyle=1;fontSize=12;" value="Simulator choice — and why not the flashy one" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="330" width="680" x="1060" y="100" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p1" parent="pick" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=8;fontStyle=1" value="✅ Gazebo Harmonic — OUR CHOICE
native ROS 2 via ros_gz_bridge · realistic sensor plugins · large world library
Our deployed nav stack IS ROS 2-native, and we need LAYOUT AND TRAFFIC, not photorealism." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="62" width="640" x="20" y="44" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p2" parent="pick" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="🟡 Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab — best for digital twins + SYNTHETIC PERCEPTION DATA
open-sourced 2025 · PhysX + RTX · OpenUSD · ROS 2 Bridge
⚠ needs an NVIDIA GPU we do not have. Reserve for ONE purpose: synthetic shelf images if C05's gallery is weak." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="66" width="640" x="20" y="114" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p3" parent="pick" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="🟡 MuJoCo / MJX — contact-rich manipulation, VLA evaluation → only relevant to R08
⚠ RGB-D and 3D LiDAR need manual setup as of Jan 2026; rendering functional, not photorealistic" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="52" width="640" x="20" y="188" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="p4" parent="pick" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=8;" value="🟡 Genie Sim 3.0 (AgibotTech/genie_sim) — Isaac-integrated, Sim2Real zero-shot benchmarks
⚠ MPL-2.0 on geniesim_* and data_collection; scene_reconstruction MULTI-LICENSED. MPL is file-level copyleft — read it.
🟡 O3DE — Apache-2.0 + MIT, game-engine rendering without NVIDIA lock-in · 🟡 Genesis — multi-physics newcomer" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="66" width="640" x="20" y="248" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bound" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=10;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=8;fontStyle=1" value="FIDELITY BOUNDARY — state it explicitly

"Gazebo worlds aren't always accurate representations of reality,
which complicates testing vision-based algorithms."

So the twin answers NAVIGATION, TRAFFIC and CAPACITY questions.
It does NOT validate perception accuracy — that is C05's job, on real images.

Re-calibrate speeds and service times from real robot logs the moment one is available.
The physical world needs tuning a minimal model cannot see." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="180" width="680" x="1060" y="470" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="cap" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fffdf5;strokeColor=#d6b656;fontSize=11;align=left;spacingLeft=10;verticalAlign=middle;" value="Cap the scope: ONE store, ONE week of replayed workload, THREE questions —
how many robots, where do they deadlock, what does it cost. Otherwise this becomes a research project." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="80" width="680" x="1060" y="670" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="demo" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f3faf1;strokeColor=#82b366;fontSize=12;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=middle;fontStyle=1" value="Demo: run with 1 robot → 95th-percentile task latency 71 minutes. Run with 3 → 18 minutes. "Three robots, and here is the curve."
Then: deadlock heatmap lights one corridor → enable an RMF mutex group → it clears. Then: turn on trading-hours customer density → scan time doubles → "which is why it runs off-peak."" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="1700" x="40" y="790" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="e1" edge="1" parent="1" source="world" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=2;exitX=0.5;exitY=1;exitDx=0;exitDy=0;entryX=0.5;entryY=0;entryDx=0;entryDy=0;" target="rob" value=""> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="e2" edge="1" parent="1" source="rob" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=2;exitX=0.5;exitY=1;exitDx=0;exitDy=0;entryX=0.5;entryY=0;entryDx=0;entryDy=0;" target="fleet" value=""> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="e3" edge="1" parent="1" source="work" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=3;exitX=0;exitY=0.5;exitDx=0;exitDy=0;entryX=1;entryY=0.35;entryDx=0;entryDy=0;labelBackgroundColor=#ffffff;fontSize=10;" target="fleet" value="tasks"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="e4" edge="1" parent="1" source="work" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;strokeColor=#9673a6;strokeWidth=3;exitX=0.5;exitY=1;exitDx=0;exitDy=0;entryX=0.5;entryY=0;entryDx=0;entryDy=0;" target="ans" value=""> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="e5" edge="1" parent="1" source="pick" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;strokeColor=#b85450;strokeWidth=2;dashed=1;exitX=0.5;exitY=1;exitDx=0;exitDy=0;entryX=0.5;entryY=0;entryDx=0;entryDy=0;" target="bound" value=""> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div:
✅ Gazebo Harmonic — OUR CHOICE
native ROS 2 via ros_gz_bridge · realistic sensor plugins · large world library
Our deployed nav stack IS ROS 2-native, and we need LAYOUT AND TRAFFIC, not photorealism.

⚠ needs an NVIDIA GPU we do not have. Reserve for ONE purpose: synthetic shelf images if C05's gallery is weak.

div.div:
FIDELITY BOUNDARY — state it explicitly
"Gazebo worlds aren't always accurate representations of reality,
which complicates testing vision-based algorithms."
So the twin answers NAVIGATION, TRAFFIC and CAPACITY questions.
It does NOT validate perception accuracy — that is C05's job, on real images.
Re-calibrate speeds and service times from real robot logs the moment one is available.
The physical world needs tuning a minimal model cannot see.

div.div:
Cap the scope: ONE store, ONE week of replayed workload, THREE questions —
how many robots, where do they deadlock, what does it cost. Otherwise this becomes a research project.

div.div:
Demo: run with 1 robot → 95th-percentile task latency 71 minutes. Run with 3 → 18 minutes. "Three robots, and here is the curve."
Then: deadlock heatmap lights one corridor → enable an RMF mutex group → it clears. Then: turn on trading-hours customer density → scan time doubles → "which is why it runs off-peak."
